A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TimeRewarder study and support comparison of the complete text, equations, Figures 1–20, Tables 1–2, and Appendix A. The appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.4 report original Meta-World reinforcement-learning evaluations, human-video transfer experiments, ablations, and ManiSkill3 PushCube-v1 results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including VOC measurements, success-rate curves, cross-domain experiments, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The temporal-distance model, weighted pair sampling, implicit negatives, two-hot loss, visual backbone, and reward construction are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten Meta-World tasks, human demonstrations under fixed and varying viewpoints for three tasks, and ManiSkill3 PushCube-v1. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including GVL in the VOC evaluation and TemporalOT, ORCA, and BCO in appendix comparisons. Rewording the explanation for excluding Rank2Reward and PROGRESSOR from VOC retains their existing exclusion.

E3.justification: Demonstration counts, held-out evaluation, GVL few-shot settings, training budgets, metrics, reward combinations, and DrQ-v2 settings are retained. Appendix A.5 and both hyperparameter tables are identical.

E4.justification: The component ablations, reward-weight and bin-count sensitivity studies, backbone comparisons, proxy-only evaluation, and PROGRESSOR negative-sampling analysis are unchanged. The trajectory case studies and representation analysis also match.

E5.justification: Both versions report learning curves as mean ± standard deviation over eight seeds. Run-count information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The VOC values in Figure 3, learning curves in Figures 6–8 and 12–20, and qualitative trajectory and representation findings are unchanged. No numerical results, rankings, or result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, the deterministic-MDP justification and visual-state assumptions in Section 4.3, and the VIP-loss unboundedness derivation in Appendix A.3 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about temporal-progress reward learning, performance on nine of ten Meta-World tasks, sample efficiency, and learning from human videos.

C2.justification: Interpretations of suboptimal behavior, representations, baseline performance, and cross-domain results are retained, along with the visual-aliasing and back-and-forth-motion limitations. The revised VOC exclusion sentence restates the existing distinction between rewards and values.

D1.justification: v3 newly provides a project-page address in the abstract. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the supplied PDFs do not establish whether code or data availability changed.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged. The Ramos et al. (2023) reference changes title but retains the same authors and arXiv:2306.09805, constituting a bibliographic update rather than a different cited work.

P1.justification: v3 adds the project-page sentence, rewords the VOC exclusion explanation, expands funding and reviewer acknowledgments, updates one reference title, and replaces the preprint notice with ICML proceedings information. Section organization and the scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The added abstract text, proceedings notice, and longer acknowledgments cause limited column and page reflow, including redistribution of references. Figure and table designs, captions, and numbering are retained; appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The added project-page pointer and explicit funding/support acknowledgments modestly improve discoverability and transparency. These are limited documentation gains; the scientific arguments, experiments, results, and appendices remain unchanged.
